introduction: “The thirsty one must run after the water; the fountain will not run after those who are thirsty.” The guide opens there, and its first readings are about thirst: it has to be developed before the water of life can do anything. The rest identify that water with the Word of God, flowing from the Pen in letters and tablets; summon people to drink; grieve over those who turn from it to a mirage; pray for it; and ask those who have drunk to give others to drink. Water is the oldest picture in scripture for this, and the Psalms, Isaiah, Jeremiah, the Gospel of John, Revelation and the Qur’an supply most of the company. The quotations that stand against the readings begin with the Dhammapada, for which thirst is the cause of suffering and not its cure. Seneca would have us want less, the Preacher doubts that any sea is ever filled, Coleridge’s mariner dies of thirst amid water, and Marcus Aurelius looks for the fountain within.
questions: The first readings say that thirst must come before the water. What has made you thirsty in this sense, and what has dulled it?
The Dhammapada counts thirst as the root of sorrow, and Seneca calls the one who craves more poor. How is the thirst praised here different from craving?
Most of these readings find the water of life in revealed words. Paul warns that the letter kills, and Proverbs says to drink from one’s own cistern. What makes reading a way of drinking?
Jeremiah’s broken cisterns and the Qur’an’s mirage describe people who go elsewhere for water. What are the cisterns and mirages of your own surroundings?
John records that Jesus, who offered living water, said “I thirst”. What does that suggest about those who are asked to give others to drink?
The last readings say the spring stays sweet by flowing. To whom, this week, could you carry a cup?

outside.why: Isaiah's invitation also asks the thirsty to move: ho, every one that thirsteth, come ye to the waters.
Emily Dickinson put the same law in five words: water is taught by thirst.
Jesus blessed those who hunger and thirst after righteousness, for they shall be filled.

The Dhammapada treats thirst as the root of suffering: it grows like a creeper, and whoever it overcomes finds his sorrows increase. How is the thirst these readings cultivate different from the thirst the Buddha taught his followers to end?
Jesus told the woman at the well that the water he gives becomes in a person a well of water springing up into everlasting life.
Proverbs says that the mouth of a righteous man is a well of life.
The Qur’an says that water is sent down from the sky and the valleys flow each according to its measure.
Hopkins ends a poem of dryness with the prayer: mine, O thou lord of life, send my roots rain.
The Qur’an says of the creation of the heavens and the earth: We made every living thing of water.
Moses says: my doctrine shall drop as the rain, my speech shall distil as the dew.
Isaiah compares the word of God to rain and snow that water the earth and do not return until it has brought forth.
Paul warned that the letter kills and only the spirit gives life. When do written words carry living water, and when are they only letters?
The first psalm likens the one who meditates in the law to a tree planted by rivers of water.
Proverbs advises: drink waters out of thine own cistern, and running waters out of thine own well. Is the fountain in a book, or does the book open a spring in the reader?
Jesus said that heaven and earth shall pass away, but his words shall not pass away.
Proverbs says that the words of a man's mouth are as deep waters, and the wellspring of wisdom as a flowing brook.
Ezekiel saw a river issuing from the sanctuary, and on its banks trees whose leaf does not fade.
The psalm says of God's words that they are more to be desired than gold, and sweeter than honey.
In the desert God opened Hagar's eyes, and she saw a well of water that had been there.
The psalm speaks of a river whose streams make glad the city of God.
The Qur’an points to the barren earth that thrills and swells when water is sent down upon it.
Paul quotes the word to Moses: I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy. If He quickens whom He wills, what is left to the one who thirsts?
The voice in Revelation says: I will give unto him that is athirst of the fountain of the water of life freely.
The last vision of the Bible is of a pure river of water of life, clear as crystal.
Zechariah foresees a day when living waters shall go out from Jerusalem, in summer and in winter.
The psalm says: Thou shalt make them drink of the river of Thy pleasures.
In the wilderness Moses struck the rock, and water came out of it for the people to drink.
The psalm says of the just king that he shall come down like rain upon the mown grass.
The psalm invites: O taste and see that the Lord is good.
The Preacher observed that all the rivers run into the sea, yet the sea is not full. Is there a water that satisfies, or is it in the nature of desire to remain unfilled?
Paul says that the fathers all drank the same spiritual drink, from a spiritual rock that followed them.
Augustine confessed that God was within him while he sought outside: Thou wert with me, and I was not with Thee. Where is the chalice offered?
Coleridge's mariner had water everywhere and not a drop to drink. What makes abundance useless to the one in the middle of it?
The psalm says that He satisfies the longing soul and fills the hungry soul with goodness.
The Qur’an says that in the remembrance of God hearts find rest.
This is the chapter of the Qur’an named for Kawthar: We have given thee Abundance.
The Qur’an names among the drinks of paradise a spring called Salsabil.
The shepherd psalm says: He leadeth me beside the still waters; He restoreth my soul.
Jeremiah calls the Lord the hope of Israel and the fountain of living waters.
Ezekiel was told to prophesy to the dry bones, and breath came into them and they lived.
John's Gospel records that the one who offered living water said from the cross: I thirst. What does it mean that the giver of the water knew thirst himself?
In the parable the rich man begs for a finger dipped in water to cool his tongue.
Amos foresaw people wandering from sea to sea to seek the word of the Lord, and fainting for thirst.
Isaiah promises that when the poor and needy seek water, rivers will be opened in high places.
Jeremiah says that his people have forsaken the fountain of living waters and hewn out broken cisterns that hold no water.
James asks whether a fountain sends forth at the same place sweet water and bitter. How can the same word be life to one hearer and bitterness to another?
The Qur’an likens the deeds of those who disbelieve to a mirage that the thirsty man takes for water until he comes to it.
Proverbs has folly say that stolen waters are sweet, and adds that her guests are in the depths of hell.
The second letter of Peter calls false teachers wells without water, and clouds carried with a tempest.
Jesus thanked the Father that these things are hidden from the wise and prudent and revealed to babes.
Jesus says: he that cometh to me shall never hunger, and he that believeth on me shall never thirst.
The psalmist says: Thou preparest a table before me; my cup runneth over.
FitzGerald's Omar asks for another cup: a jug of wine, a loaf of bread and a companion, and calls that paradise enough. What does his cup offer, and what does it leave out?
Isaiah hears: I will pour water upon him that is thirsty, and floods upon the dry ground.
The Bible closes with the invitation: whosoever will, let him take the water of life freely.
Seneca held that the poor man is the one who craves more, and that wisdom lies in wanting little. Is the command to drink a command to desire more, or to desire one thing?
Elijah asked the people on Carmel how long they would halt between two opinions.
The Qur’an speaks of a pure wine, sealed, given to the righteous to drink.
Isaiah promises the stranger a place in God's house, which shall be called a house of prayer for all people.
The psalmist says: as the hart panteth after the water brooks, so panteth my soul after Thee.
The psalmist says: my soul thirsteth for Thee in a dry and thirsty land, where no water is.
The psalm says: with Thee is the fountain of life; in Thy light shall we see light.
Emerson distrusted any prayer that craves a particular commodity, and counted only the contemplation of the highest good as prayer. What is being asked for when a prayer asks for living water?
The psalmist says: I will lift up mine eyes unto the hills; my help cometh from the Lord.
Isaiah says: with joy shall ye draw water out of the wells of salvation.
In Revelation the redeemed thirst no more, for the Lamb leads them to living fountains of waters.
The psalm speaks of pilgrims who pass through the valley of weeping and make it a well.
The prayer that Jesus taught his disciples asks each day for no more than that day's bread.
Augustine prayed: Thou hast made us for Thyself, and our hearts are restless until they rest in Thee.
Isaiah says of the servant that a bruised reed he shall not break, and the smoking flax he shall not quench.
Isaiah promises: thou shalt be like a watered garden, and like a spring of water whose waters fail not.
Ten lepers were healed, and one turned back to give thanks. How much of thirst that has been quenched remembers to give praise?
Habakkuk foresees the earth filled with the knowledge of the Lord's glory as the waters cover the sea.
The Qur’an asks whether one whose bosom God has expanded, so that he follows a light, is like the hard of heart.
In the parable some seed fell on good ground and brought forth a hundredfold.
The merchant in the parable sold all that he had for one pearl, and counted it a good bargain.
Jesus told his disciples that many prophets desired to see what they saw.
In the parable some receive the word with joy and wither when the sun is up, having no root. What keeps a person who has drunk from falling away?
James asks his readers to be doers of the word and not hearers only.
Jesus says that whoever hears and believes has passed from death unto life.
The psalm of return says: the Lord hath done great things for us, whereof we are glad.
The Song of Songs speaks of a fountain of gardens, a well of living waters.
Old Simeon took the child in his arms and said that his eyes had seen what he waited for.
The Qur’an says that water is sent down from the sky in measure and lodged in the earth.
Paul says: I have planted, Apollos watered, but God gave the increase.
Isaiah foresees the earth full of the knowledge of the Lord, as the waters cover the sea.
Jesus said that if his disciples held their peace, the stones would cry out.
The Tao Te Ching says that he who knows does not speak, and he who is ready to speak does not know. Is silence after drinking a failure, or sometimes the truer witness?
Proverbs says that the liberal soul shall be made fat, and he that watereth shall be watered also himself.
Jesus said that whoever gives a cup of cold water to one of these little ones shall not lose his reward.
Marcus Aurelius wrote: look within; within is the fountain of good, and it will ever bubble up if thou wilt ever dig. Does one have to wander to find the spring?
Isaiah foresees waters breaking out in the wilderness, and the desert blossoming as the rose.
The Qur’an asks: if all your water were to sink into the earth, who then could bring you gushing water?
The Chandogya Upanishad speaks of rivers that run east and west and become the sea.
Heraclitus said that fresh waters are ever flowing in upon those who step into the same rivers. Why does a spring stay sweet only while it flows?
Proverbs says that good news from a far country is as cold waters to a thirsty soul.
Paul asks how people shall believe in one of whom they have not heard, and how hear without a preacher.
Elisha cast salt into a bad spring and said: I have healed these waters.
At Marah a single tree cast into the bitter waters made them sweet.
Jesus cried out at the feast: if any man thirst, let him come unto me and drink, and out of him shall flow rivers of living water.

john-if-any-man-thirst.text: In the last day, that great day of the feast, Jesus stood and cried, saying, If any man thirst, let him come unto me, and drink. He that believeth on me, as the scripture hath said, out of his belly shall flow rivers of living water

isaiah-every-one-that-thirsteth.text: Ho, every one that thirsteth, come ye to the waters, and he that hath no money; come ye, buy, and eat; yea, come, buy wine and milk without money and without price. Wherefore do ye spend money for that which is not bread? and your labour for that which satisfieth not? hearken diligently unto me, and eat ye that which is good, and let your soul delight itself in fatness

isaiah-wells-of-salvation.text: Therefore with joy shall ye draw water out of the wells of salvation

isaiah-poor-and-needy-seek-water.text: When the poor and needy seek water, and there is none, and their tongue faileth for thirst, I the Lord will hear them, I the God of Israel will not forsake them. I will open rivers in high places, and fountains in the midst of the valleys: I will make the wilderness a pool of water, and the dry land springs of water

isaiah-watered-garden.text: And the Lord shall guide thee continually, and satisfy thy soul in drought, and make fat thy bones: and thou shalt be like a watered garden, and like a spring of water, whose waters fail not

jeremiah-fountain-of-living-waters.text: O Lord, the hope of Israel, all that forsake thee shall be ashamed, and they that depart from me shall be written in the earth, because they have forsaken the Lord, the fountain of living waters

zechariah-living-waters-shall-go-out.text: And it shall be in that day, that living waters shall go out from Jerusalem; half of them toward the former sea, and half of them toward the hinder sea: in summer and in winter shall it be

revelation-fountains-of-waters.text: They shall hunger no more, neither thirst any more; neither shall the sun light on them, nor any heat. For the Lamb which is in the midst of the throne shall feed them, and shall lead them unto living fountains of waters: and God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes

revelation-athirst-freely.text: And he said unto me, It is done. I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end. I will give unto him that is athirst of the fountain of the water of life freely

matthew-hunger-and-thirst.text: Blessed are they which do hunger and thirst after righteousness: for they shall be filled

psalm-still-waters.text: The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want. He maketh me to lie down in green pastures: he leadeth me beside the still waters. He restoreth my soul: he leadeth me in the paths of righteousness for his name's sake

psalm-river-make-glad.text: There is a river, the streams whereof shall make glad the city of God, the holy place of the tabernacles of the most High

psalm-satisfieth-the-longing-soul.text: For he satisfieth the longing soul, and filleth the hungry soul with goodness

psalm-river-of-thy-pleasures.text: They shall be abundantly satisfied with the fatness of thy house; and thou shalt make them drink of the river of thy pleasures

psalm-valley-of-baca.text: Blessed is the man whose strength is in thee; in whose heart are the ways of them. Who passing through the valley of Baca make it a well; the rain also filleth the pools

proverbs-watereth-shall-be-watered.text: The liberal soul shall be made fat: and he that watereth shall be watered also himself

proverbs-well-of-life.text: The mouth of a righteous man is a well of life: but violence covereth the mouth of the wicked

proverbs-deep-waters.text: The words of a man's mouth are as deep waters, and the wellspring of wisdom as a flowing brook

proverbs-stolen-waters.text: Stolen waters are sweet, and bread eaten in secret is pleasant. But he knoweth not that the dead are there; and that her guests are in the depths of hell

proverbs-thine-own-cistern.text: Drink waters out of thine own cistern, and running waters out of thine own well

exodus-waters-of-marah.text: And when they came to Marah, they could not drink of the waters of Marah, for they were bitter: therefore the name of it was called Marah. And the people murmured against Moses, saying, What shall we drink? And he cried unto the Lord; and the Lord shewed him a tree, which when he had cast into the waters, the waters were made sweet

exodus-water-out-of-the-rock.text: And the Lord said unto Moses, Go on before the people, and take with thee of the elders of Israel

genesis-hagar-well-of-water.text: And God opened her eyes, and she saw a well of water; and she went, and filled the bottle with water, and gave the lad drink

john-i-thirst.text: After this, Jesus knowing that all things were now accomplished, that the scripture might be fulfilled, saith, I thirst

luke-cool-my-tongue.text: And he cried and said, Father Abraham, have mercy on me, and send Lazarus, that he may dip the tip of his finger in water, and cool my tongue; for I am tormented in this flame

james-sweet-water-and-bitter.text: Doth a fountain send forth at the same place sweet water and bitter? Can the fig tree, my brethren, bear olive berries? either a vine, figs? so can no fountain both yield salt water and fresh

song-fountain-of-gardens.text: A fountain of gardens, a well of living waters, and streams from Lebanon

kings-healed-these-waters.text: And he went forth unto the spring of the waters, and cast the salt in there, and said, Thus saith the Lord, I have healed these waters; there shall not be from thence any more death or barren land

amos-thirst-for-hearing.text: And they shall wander from sea to sea, and from the north even to the east, they shall run to and fro to seek the word of the Lord, and shall not find it. In that day shall the fair virgins and young men faint for thirst

corinthians-spiritual-rock.text: And did all eat the same spiritual meat; And did all drink the same spiritual drink: for they drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Christ

peter-wells-without-water.text: These are wells without water, clouds that are carried with a tempest; to whom the mist of darkness is reserved for ever

quran-as-a-mirage.text: As for those who disbelieve, their deeds are as a mirage in a desert. The thirsty one supposeth it to be water till he cometh unto it and findeth it naught, and findeth, in the place thereof, Allah Who payeth him his due; and Allah is swift at reckoning.

quran-spring-named-salsabil.text: There are they watered with a cup whereof the mixture is of Zanjabil, (The water of) a spring therein, named Salsabil

quran-water-from-the-sky-in-measure.text: And we send down from the sky water in measure, and We give it lodging in the earth, and lo! We are Able to withdraw it.

quran-if-your-water-were-to-disappear.text: Say: Have ye thought: If (all) your water were to disappear into the earth, who then could bring you gushing water?

dickinson-water-is-taught-by-thirst.text: WATER is taught by thirst; / Land, by the oceans passed; / Transport, by throe; / Peace, by its battles told; / Love, by memorial mould; / Birds, by the snow
dickinson-water-is-taught-by-thirst.author: Emily Dickinson

coleridge-water-water-every-where.text: Water, water, every where, / And all the boards did shrink; / Water, water, every where, / Nor any drop to drink
coleridge-water-water-every-where.author: Samuel Taylor Coleridge
coleridge-water-water-every-where.work: The Rime of the Ancient Mariner

dhammapada-thirst-like-a-creeper.text: The thirst of a thoughtless man grows like a creeper; he runs from life to life, like a monkey seeking fruit in the forest. Whomsoever this fierce thirst overcomes, full of poison, in this world, his sufferings increase like the abounding Birana grass

dhammapada-from-thirst-comes-grief.text: From greed comes grief, from greed comes fear; he who is free from greed knows neither grief nor fear
